title: Spectral Theory of Semisimple Bivariate Bicycle Codes
authors: Eric Sabo, Mahir Bilen Can, David Marquis
abstract: Extending the classical theory of two-dimensional cyclic codes, we develop an algebraic approach to bivariate bicycle codes. Using Frobenius-orbit idempotents, formulas for logical dimensions are derived and lower bounds on minimum distances are established. A systematic theory of code symmetries is formulated to construct a structured block-monomial subgroup of coordinate permutations. Several explicit examples show how to generate these codes from first principles without relying on numerical searches. An appendix extends the analysis to BCH-based product constructions.
summary: This paper introduces an algebraic framework to systematically study bivariate bicycle codes, which are crucial for quantum error correction. By employing advanced tools from commutative algebra, the authors derive exact formulas for code dimensions and establish rigorous lower bounds on the quantum minimum distance. This moves the field beyond numerical searches toward deterministic code construction.
main_problem: The paper develops an algebraic method to analyze bivariate bicycle (BB) codes, which are identified as a leading family of quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes.
main_result: The authors derive systematic, computable formulas for the logical dimension and establish sharper, computable lower bounds on the quantum minimum distance for these codes.
method: The approach uses advanced tools from commutative algebra, including decomposing the defining ring using Frobenius-orbit idempotents and analyzing code structures as ideals in group algebras.
model_or_system: The model is the algebraic structure of bivariate bicycle codes, which are used to construct quantum error-correcting codes (QLDPC codes) for near-term quantum computing architectures.
key_observables: Logical dimension, quantum minimum distance ($d_Z$), and the structure of code symmetries (automorphisms).
important_parameters: The defining ring $R = 	ext{F}_q[x, y]/\langle x^{\ell-1}, y^{m-1} angle$, and the parameters $\ell$ and $m$ defining the code structure.
main_assumptions: The analysis is most straightforward for coprime BB codes, and the method provides bounds rather than the exact distance.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the algebraic framework by relating BB codes to 2D cyclic codes, deriving dimension formulas via orbit decomposition, establishing duality, and finally calculating distance bounds using colon-ideal refinements.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between algebraic coding theory (semisimple algebras, ideals) and the construction of QLDPC codes provides a powerful, deterministic tool for designing quantum error correction codes.
